title: Why Proper Pipe Sizing Matters in Water Supply Systems
description: An educational guide explaining how undersized supply pipes lead to dynamic pressure loss, friction buildup, and reduced fixture performance.
image_prompt: A professional 9:16 vertical educational technical illustration showing a longitudinal cross-section cutaway of two water supply pipes side-by-side against a clean studio background. The left pipe is a 1/2-inch copper pipe showing narrow internal volume with dense fluid flow lines indicating high friction resistance. The right pipe is a 3/4-inch copper pipe showing spacious internal volume with balanced flow lines representing smooth water volume distribution. Realistic metal textures, clean brass connections, photorealistic rendering, neutral lighting, soft shadows. Main plumbing components centered visually with clean space at top and bottom for text overlays. No text, no arrows, no watermarks, no logos, no fake labels.
visual_story: The visual compares an undersized supply pipe cutaway against a correctly sized trunk line cutaway. Viewers notice how internal pipe diameter directly affects physical water volume space and friction resistance inside the line. This demonstrates why opening a tap elsewhere in a building drops pressure if the main feeding pipe lacks sufficient volumetric capacity.

on_image_text.explanation: Pipes sized too small create high internal friction loss, severely restricting water flow volume during peak demand.
on_image_text.takeaway: Size main supply trunks based on total fixture units before branching to individual lines.
